achieve.ex: She worked hard to achieve her goals.

activity.en: work being done in an area
activity.ex: Economic activity slowed during the winter.

adds.ex: He adds that the plan needs more money.

advice.en: ideas about what someone should do
advice.ex: My teacher gave me good advice about exams.

advises.en: tells someone what they should do
advises.ex: The doctor advises him to rest for a week.

advisory.ex: She sits on an advisory board for the school.

again.ex: The team lost again on Saturday.

agricultural.ex: Agricultural land covers most of the region.

ahead.ex: We have a busy week ahead.
ahead.zh: in the years ahead：在未來幾年

aim.ex: Her aim is to finish the course this year.

also.ex: She speaks French and also some German.

alternative.en: another thing you can use instead
alternative.ex: Cycling is a cheap alternative to driving.

anaerobic.ex: Anaerobic bacteria break down the waste in tanks.

and.en: used to join words or ideas

anticipated.ex: Sales are anticipated to rise next year.

example.en: Prices are anticipated to fall next spring.
example.zh: 預計明年春天物價將下跌。

note.usage: 常用 be anticipated to do 或 anticipate + 名詞／that 子句；比 expect 更正式。

noteEn.meaning: to expect that something will happen.
noteEn.usage: Often passive: 'be anticipated to + verb'; more formal than 'expect'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Se prevé que los precios bajen la próxima primavera.
noteEs.meaning: prever o esperar que algo ocurra.
noteEs.usage: Es común be anticipated to + verbo; es más formal que expect.

noteHi.exampleTr: अगले वसंत में कीमतें गिरने का अनुमान है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी बात के होने की उम्मीद या अनुमान करना।
noteHi.usage: be anticipated to do आम है; यह expect से अधिक औपचारिक है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 来春には物価が下がると予想されている。
noteJa.meaning: 何かが起こると予想する。
noteJa.usage: be anticipated to do の形が多く、expect より改まった語。

noteKo.exampleTr: 내년 봄에는 물가가 내릴 것으로 예상된다.
noteKo.usage: be anticipated to do 형태가 흔하며 expect보다 격식 있는 말이다.

are.en: form of 'be' used with plural subjects

areas.ex: Some areas of science need more funding.

assessment.ex: The doctor made a careful assessment of his health.

at.en: used to show a point in time

badly.en: very much; in a serious way
badly.ex: The project is badly behind schedule.

baseline.ex: We used last year's sales as a baseline.

behind.ex: The builders are two weeks behind.

benchmark.en: a standard used to compare things
benchmark.ex: These results set a new benchmark for the industry.

big.ex: Traffic is a big problem in the city.

biomethane.en: gas made from rotting farm and food waste
biomethane.ex: The farm turns animal waste into biomethane.

body.ex: An independent body will check the election.

build.ex: They plan to build a new school here.

builders.en: people or firms that make buildings
builders.ex: The builders finished the house in June.

building.en: the work of making houses and structures

buildings.en: structures such as houses or offices

burgeoning.ex: The city has a burgeoning tech scene.

by.en: showing amount of change or a time limit

cancel.ex: Higher prices could cancel the benefit of the tax cut.

cement.en: grey powder used to make concrete
cement.ex: The workers mixed cement with sand and water.

cent.en: used in 'per cent' meaning out of 100
cent.ex: Prices rose by five per cent.

change.en: in 'climate change': change in world weather

characterised.en: described as having a certain quality
characterised.ex: Critics characterised the film as boring.

clear.ex: The sign gave a clear message to drivers.

climate.en: the usual weather of the world or a place
climate.ex: The climate here is warm and dry.

coming.ex: Prices may rise in the coming months.

compared.ex: This year is colder compared with last year.

compelling.ex: The lawyer presented compelling proof of his innocence.

example.en: There is compelling evidence that exercise improves mood.
example.zh: 有令人信服的證據顯示運動能改善心情。

note.meaning: 非常有說服力、讓人無法忽視的。
note.usage: 常修飾 evidence、argument、reason 等名詞；正式文章中很常見。

noteEn.meaning: very strong and convincing; hard to ignore.

noteEs.exampleTr: Hay pruebas contundentes de que el ejercicio mejora el estado de ánimo.
noteEs.usage: Suele acompañar a evidence, argument o reason.

noteHi.exampleTr: इस बात के ठोस प्रमाण हैं कि व्यायाम मूड को बेहतर बनाता है।
noteHi.meaning: बहुत ठोस और विश्वसनीय, जिसे नज़रअंदाज़ न किया जा सके।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर evidence, argument, reason के साथ आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 運動が気分を良くするという説得力のある証拠がある。
noteJa.meaning: 非常に説得力があり、無視できない。
noteJa.usage: evidence、argument、reason などの名詞を修飾することが多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 운동이 기분을 좋게 한다는 설득력 있는 증거가 있다.
noteKo.usage: evidence, argument, reason 같은 명사를 자주 수식한다.

concludes.ex: The study concludes that sleep helps memory.

concrete.en: hard building material made with cement
concrete.ex: The bridge is made of steel and concrete.

consequence.ex: He lost his job as a consequence of his mistakes.
consequence.zh: as a consequence of：由於…的結果

consequently.ex: The road was closed; consequently, we were late.

example.en: Demand fell; consequently, the factory cut jobs.
example.zh: 需求下降，因此工廠裁減了職位。

note.meaning: 因此、所以；表示前述情況造成的結果。
note.usage: 常放句首或分號後，後接逗號；比 so 正式，多用於書面語。

noteEn.meaning: as a result of what was just said.
noteEn.usage: Often at the start of a clause or after a semicolon; more formal than 'so'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La demanda cayó; por consiguiente, la fábrica recortó empleos.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir al inicio de la oración o tras punto y coma; es más formal que so.

noteHi.exampleTr: माँग घट गई; परिणामस्वरूप, कारख़ाने ने नौकरियाँ कम कर दीं।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर वाक्य की शुरुआत में या अर्धविराम के बाद आता है; so से अधिक औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 需要が落ち込んだ。その結果、工場は人員を削減した。
noteJa.meaning: その結果として；したがって。
noteJa.usage: 文頭やセミコロンの後に置くことが多く、so より改まった書き言葉。

noteKo.exampleTr: 수요가 줄었고, 그 결과 공장은 일자리를 줄였다.
noteKo.usage: 문장 앞이나 세미콜론 뒤에 자주 쓰며 so보다 격식 있는 문어체이다.

considerably.ex: The new road is considerably faster.

constraint.en: something that limits what you can do
constraint.ex: Lack of money is a major constraint on the project.

construction.ex: He works in construction as an engineer.

contingent.ex: The trip is contingent on good weather.

example.en: Our plans are contingent on the weather.
example.zh: 我們的計畫取決於天氣。

note.usage: 固定搭配 be contingent on/upon sth，多用於正式或商業文件。

noteEn.meaning: depending on something else happening first.
noteEn.usage: Use 'be contingent on/upon something'; it is formal.

noteEs.meaning: que depende de otra cosa; condicionado.
noteEs.usage: Se usa be contingent on/upon, sobre todo en textos formales.

noteHi.exampleTr: हमारी योजनाएँ मौसम पर निर्भर हैं।
noteHi.meaning: किसी और बात पर निर्भर होना।
noteHi.usage: be contingent on/upon के रूप में, औपचारिक भाषा में प्रयोग होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 私たちの計画は天気次第だ。
noteJa.meaning: 他の事柄に左右される；〜を条件とする。
noteJa.usage: be contingent on/upon の形で、改まった文章で使う。

noteKo.meaning: 다른 일에 따라 결정되는; ~을 조건으로 하는.
noteKo.usage: be contingent on/upon 형태로 격식 있는 글에서 쓴다.

council.en: an official group that gives advice or decides
council.ex: The council meets once a month.

council's.ex: The council's decision surprised many people.

country's.ex: The country's economy grew last year.

course.en: in 'on course to': likely to happen
course.ex: The team is on course to win the league.
course.zh: on course to：可望；正朝…發展

creep.ex: Prices continue to creep up each month.

criticises.en: says what is wrong with something
criticises.ex: The report criticises the slow response.

current.ex: The current price of bread is high.

currently.ex: She is currently living in Cork.

cut.ex: The shop cut its prices by half.

decade.ex: The town changed a lot in the last decade.

deliver.ex: Solar panels deliver power to the village.

demanding.ex: Processes demanding high heat use a lot of fuel.

described.ex: She described the hotel as noisy.

digesters.en: tanks where waste breaks down to make gas
digesters.ex: The farm uses digesters to turn manure into gas.

digestion.en: process where waste breaks down to make gas
digestion.ex: Anaerobic digestion turns food waste into energy.

diminish.ex: His interest in the game began to diminish.

down.ex: House prices went down last year.

easily.ex: She can easily walk ten kilometres.

electricity.en: power used for lights and machines
electricity.ex: The storm cut off electricity to many homes.

emissions.ex: Cars produce large amounts of emissions.

emitting.ex: The factory is emitting black smoke.

end.en: the last part of a period
end.ex: We will move house at the end of the year.

energy.ex: Wind is a clean source of energy.

enough.ex: We have enough food for the trip.

even.en: in 'even though': despite the fact that

evidence.en: facts that show something is true
evidence.ex: There is no evidence that he was there.

existing.ex: The existing rules are too weak.

expanding.ex: The company is expanding into Asia.

expected.ex: The rain is expected to stop by noon.

facilities.en: buildings made for a special use
facilities.ex: The town has good sports facilities.

factories.ex: Many factories closed during the crisis.

failed.ex: He failed to finish the race.

fall.en: go down to a lower level

far.ex: The work is far behind what we planned.

farm.en: land used for growing crops and animals
farm.ex: My uncle keeps cows on his farm.

fast.ex: We need to act fast to save the forest.

flatlined.en: stopped growing; stayed at the same level
flatlined.ex: Sales have flatlined since the spring.

food.ex: We throw away too much food.

for.en: used to show purpose or who/what

forecast.ex: Heavy snow is forecast for tomorrow.

further.ex: The study further shows that diet matters.

gap.ex: The gap between rich and poor is growing.

gas.ex: We cook with gas at home.

gives.ex: She gives her time to help others.

goal.ex: Her goal is to run a marathon.

going.ex: Unemployment is going down this year.

government.en: group of people who run a country
government.ex: The government will build new homes.

government's.ex: The government's plan was announced today.

green.ex: The city wants more green energy.

greenhouse.en: in 'greenhouse gas': gas that warms the earth
greenhouse.ex: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas.

grows.ex: The town grows bigger every year.

heat.ex: The heat from the oven filled the kitchen.

help.ex: Fresh air can help you sleep.

high.ex: The oven reaches very high temperatures.

high-temperature.ex: Glass is made in high-temperature furnaces.

hurdle.en: a problem that must be overcome
hurdle.ex: Cost is the biggest hurdle for new students.

identifies.ex: The report identifies three main risks.

ill-suited.ex: These shoes are ill-suited to hiking.

impediments.ex: High costs are impediments to change.

example.en: Poor roads are a major impediment to trade.
example.zh: 糟糕的道路是貿易的一大障礙。

note.meaning: 阻礙事情進展的障礙或因素。
note.usage: 常用 an impediment to sth；為正式用語，比 obstacle 更書面。

noteEn.meaning: something that blocks or slows progress.
noteEn.usage: Use 'an impediment to something'; a formal word like 'obstacle'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las malas carreteras son un gran obstáculo para el comercio.
noteEs.meaning: algo que impide o dificulta el progreso.
noteEs.usage: Se usa an impediment to sth; es una palabra formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: ख़राब सड़कें व्यापार में एक बड़ी बाधा हैं।
noteHi.meaning: ऐसी चीज़ जो प्रगति को रोकती है।
noteHi.usage: an impediment to sth के रूप में; यह औपचारिक शब्द है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 道路の悪さは貿易の大きな障害だ。
noteJa.meaning: 物事の進展を妨げるもの。
noteJa.usage: an impediment to sth の形で使う改まった語。

noteKo.usage: an impediment to sth 형태로 쓰는 격식 있는 말이다.

example.en: The old bridge is inadequate for heavy trucks.
example.zh: 這座舊橋不足以承載重型卡車。

note.meaning: 不足夠的、不夠好的，無法滿足需要。
note.usage: 常用 be inadequate to do／for sth；常修飾 regulation、funding、supply 等。

noteEn.meaning: not enough or not good enough for a need.
noteEn.usage: Use 'inadequate for something' or 'inadequate to do something'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El viejo puente no es adecuado para camiones pesados.
noteEs.meaning: no suficiente o no lo bastante bueno.
noteEs.usage: Se usa be inadequate to do / for sth; frecuente con funding o regulation.

noteHi.exampleTr: पुराना पुल भारी ट्रकों के लिए अपर्याप्त है।
noteHi.meaning: ज़रूरत के हिसाब से काफ़ी या अच्छा नहीं।
noteHi.usage: be inadequate to do / for sth; funding, regulation आदि के साथ आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: 古い橋は大型トラックには不十分だ。
noteJa.meaning: 必要を満たすには不十分な。
noteJa.usage: be inadequate to do / for sth の形が多く、funding や regulation などを修飾する。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 낡은 다리는 대형 트럭이 다니기에 부적합하다.
noteKo.usage: be inadequate to do / for sth 형태가 많고 funding, regulation 등을 수식한다.

indicates.ex: The test indicates that the water is safe.

industrial.ex: The river runs through an industrial area.

industry.en: factories and businesses that make goods
industry.ex: Tourism is a big industry in Spain.

insufficient.ex: There was insufficient time to finish.

example.en: The money was insufficient to repair the roof.
example.zh: 那筆錢不足以修好屋頂。

note.meaning: 數量或程度不足，不夠用。
note.usage: 比 not enough 正式；常用 insufficient to do 或 insufficient + 名詞。

noteEn.meaning: not enough in amount or degree.
noteEn.usage: More formal than 'not enough'; use 'insufficient to do' or before a noun.

noteEs.exampleTr: El dinero era insuficiente para reparar el tejado.
noteEs.meaning: no suficiente en cantidad o grado.
noteEs.usage: Más formal que not enough; se usa insufficient to + verbo o insufficient + sustantivo.

noteHi.exampleTr: छत की मरम्मत के लिए पैसे अपर्याप्त थे।
noteHi.meaning: मात्रा या स्तर में पर्याप्त नहीं।
noteHi.usage: not enough से अधिक औपचारिक; insufficient to do या insufficient + संज्ञा।

noteJa.exampleTr: そのお金では屋根を修理するのに足りなかった。
noteJa.usage: not enough より改まった言い方で、insufficient to do や insufficient + 名詞で使う。

noteKo.usage: not enough보다 격식 있으며 insufficient to do 또는 insufficient + 명사로 쓴다.

intense.ex: The intense heat melted the metal.

key.ex: Education is a key issue in the election.

kind.ex: What kind of music do you like?

lagging.ex: Sales are lagging behind last year's.

laments.en: says it is unhappy about something
laments.ex: He laments the loss of local shops.

large.ex: They live in a large house.

largely.ex: The town is largely quiet at night.

largest.ex: This is the largest lake in the country.

latest.ex: Have you read her latest book?

lax.ex: Security at the airport was lax.

levels.ex: Pollution levels are high in the city.

likely.ex: It is likely to rain later.

limited.ex: We have limited time before the exam.

look.ex: The weather looks fine for tomorrow.

low-carbon.ex: The city wants more low-carbon buses.

lower.ex: Prices are lower in the market.

main.ex: The main road is closed today.

major.ex: The city has three major hospitals.

make.ex: Cows make a lot of methane.

makers.ex: Car makers are moving to electric models.

example.en: The new phone is only marginally faster.

note.meaning: 微幅地、稍微地；變化很小。
note.usage: 常修飾 increase、rise 或比較級，正式程度高於 slightly。

noteEn.usage: Often with 'increase', 'rise' or comparatives; more formal than 'slightly'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El nuevo teléfono es solo ligeramente más rápido.
noteEs.usage: Acompaña a increase, rise o comparativos; más formal que slightly.

noteHi.exampleTr: नया फ़ोन बस थोड़ा-सा तेज़ है।
noteHi.usage: increase, rise या तुलनात्मक शब्दों के साथ; slightly से अधिक औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい電話はほんの少し速いだけだ。
noteJa.usage: increase、rise や比較級と使い、slightly より改まった語。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 휴대폰은 아주 약간 더 빠를 뿐이다.
noteKo.usage: increase, rise나 비교급과 함께 쓰며 slightly보다 격식 있다.

materials.ex: Wood and stone are natural building materials.

measures.en: actions taken to deal with a problem
measures.ex: New measures will reduce traffic in the city.

member.en: a person who belongs to a group
member.ex: She is a member of the tennis club.

miss.ex: We may miss our sales target this month.

missed.ex: The firm missed its profit goal.

moment.ex: I am busy at the moment.

narrow.ex: The gap between the two teams has narrowed.

necessary.ex: Is it necessary to book a table?

next.ex: We will meet again next week.

not.ex: The plan is not ready yet.

now.ex: Now the shop opens at nine.

objective.ex: Our main objective is to cut costs.

obligation.en: something you must do by law or duty
obligation.ex: Employers have an obligation to keep workers safe.

example.en: Countries have an obligation to protect the environment.
example.zh: 各國有保護環境的義務。

note.meaning: （法律、道德或合約上的）義務、責任。
note.usage: 常用 an obligation to do sth 或 be under an obligation to；legal obligation 也很常見。

noteEn.meaning: something you must do because of a law, rule or promise.
noteEn.usage: Use 'an obligation to do something'; 'legal obligation' is common.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los países tienen la obligación de proteger el medio ambiente.
noteEs.usage: Se usa an obligation to + verbo; legal obligation es frecuente.

noteHi.exampleTr: देशों का पर्यावरण की रक्षा करने का दायित्व है।
noteHi.meaning: कानून, नैतिकता या अनुबंध से बना कर्तव्य।
noteHi.usage: an obligation to do sth या legal obligation के रूप में आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 各国には環境を守る義務がある。
noteJa.meaning: 法律・道徳・契約上の義務。
noteJa.usage: an obligation to do の形や legal obligation がよく使われる。

noteKo.usage: an obligation to do 형태나 legal obligation이 자주 쓰인다.

obliged.ex: Drivers are obliged to wear seat belts.

obstacle.ex: Language can be an obstacle for new arrivals.

only.ex: There is only one bus a day.

overshot.ex: The project overshot its budget by a million euros.

own.ex: They own two houses in Spain.

plan.en: an idea of what to do
plan.ex: The city has a plan to build more parks.

plans.ex: Plans for a new airport were rejected.

plants.ex: Two power plants will close next year.

poised.ex: The team is poised to win the title.

policy.en: a plan of action by a government
policy.ex: The new policy helps young workers.

principal.ex: Rice is the principal food in the region.

problem.ex: Parking is a problem in the town centre.

processes.en: series of steps to make products
processes.ex: New processes made the factory cleaner.

produce.ex: The farm produces milk and cheese.

progress.ex: Students have made good progress this term.

projections.ex: Population projections show the city will grow.

projects.ex: The council funds many building projects.

provision.ex: The provision of clean water is vital.

rates.en: levels measured as amounts or percentages

readily.ex: Fresh fish is readily available here.

recent.ex: Recent rain has filled the lakes.

reduce.ex: We must reduce our energy use.

reduction.ex: There was a reduction in road deaths.

relative.ex: Prices are high relative to wages.

remains.ex: The museum remains closed on Mondays.

renewable.ex: Solar power is a renewable source of energy.

report.en: a written document about a subject
report.ex: The report was published on Monday.

required.ex: Visitors are required to sign in.

rise.ex: Rents rise every year in the city.

rollout.en: putting something into use in many places
rollout.ex: The rollout of fast internet took two years.

rules.en: official instructions about what is allowed
rules.ex: The school has strict rules about phones.

said.ex: She said the trip was great.

says.ex: The sign says the shop is closed.

scant.ex: He paid scant attention to the warning.

scarce.ex: Water is scarce in the desert.

example.en: Fresh vegetables are scarce here in winter.
example.zh: 這裡冬天新鮮蔬菜很稀少。

note.usage: 多作表語：sth is scarce；常形容資源、資金、食物等。

noteEn.meaning: not available in large amounts; hard to find.
noteEn.usage: Often after a verb: 'X is scarce'; used for resources, water or food.

noteEs.exampleTr: Aquí las verduras frescas escasean en invierno.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir después del verbo: sth is scarce; se usa con recursos, agua o comida.

noteHi.exampleTr: यहाँ सर्दियों में ताज़ी सब्ज़ियाँ बहुत कम मिलती हैं।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर sth is scarce के रूप में; संसाधन, पानी, भोजन के लिए।

noteJa.exampleTr: ここでは冬に新鮮な野菜が手に入りにくい。
noteJa.usage: sth is scarce の形が多く、資源・水・食料などに使う。

noteKo.usage: 주로 sth is scarce 형태로 자원, 물, 식량 등에 쓴다.

schedule.en: a plan of when things happen
schedule.ex: The train is running behind schedule.

sector.ex: She works in the health sector.

set.ex: Prices are set to rise next year.

short.ex: Food was in short supply after the storm.
short.zh: fall short：未達到；in short supply：短缺

shows.ex: The map shows the way to the station.

signal.en: a sign that tells you something
signal.ex: The price rise is a signal of trouble.

significant.ex: There was a significant rise in sales.

sits.ex: Unemployment sits at five per cent.

slash.ex: The store will slash prices this weekend.

stagnant.ex: Wages have been stagnant for years.

stagnated.ex: The economy stagnated for several years.

example.en: Her career stagnated after she stopped learning.
example.zh: 她停止學習後，事業便停滯不前。

note.usage: 不及物動詞，主詞常為 economy、wages、rates 等；形容詞形為 stagnant。

noteEn.meaning: to stop growing, changing or improving.
noteEn.usage: No object; often with 'economy', 'wages' or 'rates'. Adjective: 'stagnant'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Su carrera se estancó después de que dejó de aprender.
noteEs.meaning: dejar de crecer o mejorar; estancarse.

noteKo.exampleTr: 배움을 멈춘 뒤 그녀의 경력은 정체되었다.

paragraphs: Ireland has a plan to cut greenhouse gases from industry. But a new report says the plan is not working well.
The Climate Change Advisory Council gives advice to the government. It says factories missed their target for 2025. They will miss the target for 2030 too.
The goal is to cut these gases by 35% by 2030. Now they are 15.9% lower than in 2018. But by 2030 this may fall to 11.6%. More building work will make more gases.
Some factories need very high heat. Electricity cannot make this heat easily. Green gas can help, but there is not much of it.
Council member Jillian Mahon says Ireland must do more, and fast.

Greenhouse gas emissions from Irish industry are likely to go up in the next few years, even though they should be going down. This is the warning in a new report from the Climate Change Advisory Council, which advises the government.

The council says industry missed its target for 2025 and will probably miss its target for 2030 too. The aim is to cut emissions by 35% compared with 2018. At the moment, emissions are 15.9% lower than in 2018, but this could fall to only 11.6% by 2030. More activity in areas like construction may cancel recent progress.

One big problem is heat. Many factories need very high temperatures, and electricity cannot easily provide them. Biomethane, a kind of renewable gas, could help, but there is not enough of it. Plans to build plants that make this gas from farm and food waste are far behind.
The council also says builders should use more low-carbon concrete and wood. It adds that recycling rates have stopped rising.
Council member Jillian Mahon said the report shows that the current measures are not enough.
Emissions from Irish industry are forecast to rise over the coming years, even though they are supposed to fall, according to the Climate Change Advisory Council.

In its latest report, the Government's climate advisory body says the sector missed its 2025 reduction target and is on course to miss its 2030 goal as well. Industry is supposed to cut emissions by 35 per cent compared with 2018 levels. It is currently 15.9 per cent below that baseline, but the gap is expected to narrow to 11.6 per cent by 2030 as activity in sectors such as construction grows.

A key obstacle is the supply of energy for high-temperature processes, which electricity cannot easily deliver. The main alternative, biomethane, remains scarce, and plans for anaerobic digesters that would produce it from agricultural and food waste are well behind schedule.

The council also criticises weak regulation on low-carbon cement and concrete, limited use of timber in large buildings, and recycling rates that have flatlined. Cement makers own four of the country's five largest emitting industrial plants.
Council member Jillian Mahon said the projections were a clear warning that existing measures were insufficient.
Far from shrinking, Ireland's industrial emissions look set to creep upwards in the years ahead, the Climate Change Advisory Council has warned.

The State's climate watchdog concludes that industry has already overshot its 2025 reduction target and is poised to fall short again in 2030. The sector is obliged to slash emissions by 35 per cent relative to 2018; while it currently sits 15.9 per cent below that benchmark, burgeoning activity in construction and other sectors threatens to whittle this down to 11.6 per cent by the end of the decade.

A stubborn hurdle is the provision of energy for processes demanding intense heat, which electricity is ill-suited to supply. Biomethane, the principal substitute, is in short supply, and the rollout of anaerobic digesters to generate it from agricultural and food waste is lagging badly.
The council also laments lax rules on low-carbon cement and concrete, scant use of timber in major projects and recycling rates that have stagnated.
Council member Jillian Mahon described the projections as an unequivocal signal that current measures are inadequate to deliver the transformation required this decade.

According to the Climate Change Advisory Council, greenhouse gas emissions from Irish industry are projected to increase marginally over the coming years, notwithstanding the obligation to reduce them.

The council's assessment indicates that the sector failed to achieve its 2025 target and is likely to miss its 2030 objective. Industry is required to reduce emissions by 35 per cent relative to 2018 levels; although it is currently 15.9 per cent below this baseline, the reduction is anticipated to diminish to 11.6 per cent by 2030, largely as a consequence of expanding construction activity.

A substantial constraint is the provision of energy for high-temperature industrial processes, which electricity cannot readily supply. Biomethane, the principal alternative, remains scarce; consequently, progress is contingent upon anaerobic digestion facilities that are considerably behind schedule.
The council further identifies inadequate regulation of low-carbon construction materials, limited utilisation of timber and stagnant recycling rates as significant impediments.
Council member Jillian Mahon characterised the projections as compelling evidence that existing policy measures are insufficient to achieve the necessary transformation.
